mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in RETAIL_REC mobility from t-1w to t-0w indicates a worsening trend in consumer discretionary activity that will persist, leading to lower average RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks compared to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility recovers significantly from its recent dip, it will signal a renewed return to office-based work and associated weekday activities, driving increased foot traffic to nearby retail and recreation spots over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in its weekly mean over the two weeks following a week-on-week rise in WORKPLACES mobility of more than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility, coupled with the recent sharp drop in GROCERY_PHARM, suggests a strong and increasing preference for staying home and reduced essential outings, which will further depress discretionary retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, while RESIDENTIAL remains above 9% and GROCERY_PHARM remains below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: If local policies shift towards easing restrictions, a rebound in TRANSIT station visits will quickly translate into increased RETAIL_REC as people feel safer and have more options for travel to leisure destinations over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following a week-on-week rise in TRANSIT mobility of more than 2 points during an easing restrictions regime.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in PARKS visits from t-1w to t-0w suggests a general decrease in outdoor activity and public engagement, indicating a broader shift towards reduced non-essential outings that will negatively impact RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite a sustained decline in PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A significant and sustained drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates fewer people staying home, freeing them up for other activities, which will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as they seek out retail and recreation options.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following a two-week consecutive drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility of more than 1 point each week.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and sustained increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicates a strong return to daily commuting and office presence, which directly boosts RETAIL_REC in urban centers and commercial areas over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise by more than 1 point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite concurrent two-week increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility stabilizes after its recent sharp decline, it suggests that essential activity has found a new baseline, potentially freeing up consumer confidence and disposable time for RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks, assuming no new major policy changes.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM changes by less than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following GROCERY_PHARM stabilization (change less than 1 point week-on-week) in a steady state regime.
